title: Classic Cannabutter
desc: The foundational infusion most cannabis-cooking recipes build on.
steps: Decarb: spread ground flower on a lined baking sheet, bake at 245°F (118°C) for 30–40 min, stirring occasionally, until light brown.
Melt butter with water in a saucepan over low heat.
Stir in the decarbed flower and simmer gently at 160–200°F for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally — do not boil.
Strain through cheesecloth into a heatproof container, pressing gently to release the butter.
Refrigerate until solid, then drain off any water underneath.
dosing: A 1:1 cannabis-to-butter ratio gives a standard-strength batch. Always test with ¼–½ tsp first and wait a full 2 hours before taking more — edibles hit slower and stronger than smoking.

title: Canna-Infused Olive Oil
desc: A neutral, savory infusion great for dressings, sautéing, or drizzling.
steps: Decarboxylate the flower the same way as for cannabutter.
Combine oil and flower in a saucepan or slow cooker on the lowest setting.
Gently heat at 160–200°F for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Strain through cheesecloth, pressing lightly, then store in a sealed jar away from light.
dosing: Label the jar with total THC and the batch size so every recipe you use it in has a known dose per tablespoon.

title: No-Bake Cannabutter Bites
desc: A quick, low-effort edible using your cannabutter — no oven required.
steps: Warm the cannabutter, peanut butter, and honey together until smooth (low heat only).
Stir in oats and salt until fully combined.
Press into a lined pan and chill for at least 2 hours.
Cut into a set number of equal squares and label the batch with dose per square.
dosing: Cut into more, smaller squares than you think you need — it's much easier to eat a second piece than to undo one that's too strong.

title: Classic Weed Brownies
desc: The all-time favorite edible — dense, fudgy, and built on cannabutter.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease an 8×8" pan.
Whisk dry ingredients (flour, cocoa, salt, baking powder, sugars) in one bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the cannabutter, eggs, and vanilla together.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients gently — don't overmix.
Pour into the pan and bake 25–30 minutes, until a toothpick comes out mostly clean.
Cool at least 30 minutes before cutting into a set number of equal squares.
dosing: Dose per brownie ≈ (grams of cannabis × THC% × 1000) ÷ number of brownies. Example: 1g flower at 20% THC across 10 brownies ≈ 20mg each. Start with a light square (2–5mg) and wait 2 hours before eating more.

title: DIY Cannabis Tincture
desc: A discreet, fast-acting sublingual option — a few drops under the tongue.
ingredients: 3–12 fl oz food-grade alcohol or a carrier oil (e.g. MCT/coconut oil)
steps: Decarb the flower at 220–240°F for 30–60 minutes until lightly toasted.
Combine decarbed flower and your chosen solvent in a sealed mason jar, fully submerging the flower.
Store in a cool, dark place for at least 4 weeks, shaking once a day.
Strain through a coffee filter or cheesecloth into a dropper bottle.
dosing: Start low: a quarter dropper (~0.25mL) held under the tongue for 30 seconds before swallowing. Effects arrive faster than edibles — usually 15–30 minutes.

title: Cannabis Fruit Gummies
desc: Chewy, dosable candies made with your own tincture — no cannabis smell or taste.
ingredients: ½ tsp citric acid (optional, for tartness)
steps: Lightly grease silicone molds.
Warm water on low heat until barely simmering.
Whisk in the unflavored gelatin and flavored gelatin mix until fully dissolved.
Whisk in sugar and citric acid, then remove from heat.
Stir in the tincture once the mixture has cooled slightly.
Fill molds with a dropper, tapping out air bubbles, and refrigerate 2–3 hours until firm.
dosing: Calculate total mg THC in your tincture batch and divide evenly across all gummies made — write the date and dose on the container so it's never a guess later.
